intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians perform as the square transforms from a daytime market into a spectacular open-air food festival at dusk. Wander the labyrinthine souks of the ancient medina, haggling for spices, leather goods, and handwoven textiles just steps from your accommodation.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp in Merzouga
experiences.description: Journey to the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga for an unforgettable camel trek into the Sahara. Ride at sunset as the dunes glow amber and rose, then spend the night in a traditional Berber desert camp under a canopy of stars. Enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, sip mint tea, and wake at dawn for a breathtaking sunrise over the dunes — a once-in-a-lifetime desert experience.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back in time with a self-guided or local-guided tour of two of Marrakech's most significant historical landmarks. The 19th-century Bahia Palace dazzles with its intricate zellij tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. A short walk away, the Saadian Tombs — sealed for centuries and rediscovered in 1917 — house the ornate mausoleums of the Saadian dynasty, offering a profound glimpse into Morocco's imperial past.
experiences.location: Kasbah & Riad Zitoun districts, Medina, Marrakech

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class with a Local Family
experiences.description: Begin your morning at the vibrant Mellah spice market to hand-select fresh ingredients — saffron, ras el hanout, preserved lemons, and more. Then join a local Marrakchi family in their home kitchen to learn the art of preparing authentic dishes such as slow-cooked lamb tagine, harira soup, and honey-drenched bastilla. Sit down together to enjoy the feast you've created, paired with fresh-baked khobz bread and mint tea.

experiences.name: Ait Benhaddou Kasbah & Draa Valley Day Trip
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day excursion from Marrakech over the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass to the UNESCO World Heritage ksar of Ait Benhaddou — a stunning fortified mud-brick village used as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue into the lush Draa Valley, Morocco's longest river valley, dotted with ancient kasbahs, palm groves, and Berber villages, offering rich historical and cultural context to your Moroccan journey.
experiences.location: Ait Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Rest and settle into Hotel Aday in the Medina.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a petit taxi to Hotel Aday at 111 Derb Sidi Bouloukat (approx. 70–100 MAD / ~$7–10 USD). Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest. If hungry, grab a quick snack from a nearby street stall still open late near Jemaa el-Fna square (5-minute walk).

meals.breakfast: On the plane or skip — arrival is late night.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: Late-night street food near Jemaa el-Fna: msemen (flatbread) with honey or a bowl of harira soup from a street vendor (15–25 MAD / ~$1.50–2.50).

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Moroccan dirhams (MAD) ready for the taxi. Exchange currency at the airport or withdraw from an ATM. Hotel Aday is a budget riad in the heart of the Medina — very walkable to all major Marrakech sights.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, explore the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square (5-minute walk from hotel) in the morning calm before the crowds arrive. Visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior view, free) and stroll through the surrounding streets. Head into the souks — explore Souk Semmarine, Souk des Épices (spice market), and Souk des Teinturiers (dyers' souk) for a sensory cultural immersion. Bargaining is expected and part of the experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD / ~$7), a stunning 19th-century palace with ornate Moroccan architecture, carved cedar ceilings, and lush courtyards. Afterward, walk to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and explore the historic Lazama Synagogue (small donation appreciated). Wander through the covered market of the Mellah for local goods at lower prices than the main souks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a massive open-air spectacle — snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Enjoy dinner at the famous night market food stalls (numbered stalls — try stall #1 or #14 for grilled meats and seafood). Sip fresh-squeezed orange juice (4 MAD / ~$0.40) from the square's juice vendors.

meals.breakfast: At Hotel Aday (often included or available for ~20–30 MAD) — Moroccan bread, olive oil, amlou (almond-argan paste), mint tea.
meals.lunch: Cheap local lunch at a medina restaurant: tagine or couscous set menu for 40–60 MAD (~$4–6) at a place like Restaurant Chez Bahia near the Bahia Palace.
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna night market food stalls: grilled kefta skewers, merguez sausage, Moroccan salads, and khobz bread — full meal for 60–80 MAD (~$6–8).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina's narrow alleys are cobblestoned and uneven. Watch out for motorbikes in the souks. Bargain respectfully in the markets — start at 40–50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD / ~$7), a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917. Arrive early (opens at 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Afterward, explore the El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD / ~$7) — a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the walls and panoramic views from the ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mellah's Mouassine neighborhood and visit the free Mouassine Fountain and the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entrance ~70 MAD / ~$7) — one of the most stunning examples of Islamic architecture in North Africa, with intricate zellij tilework, carved stucco, and cedar wood. Spend time in the quieter northern Medina streets around Dar el-Bacha for a more authentic, less touristy experience.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxing walk along the Medina walls at sunset. Visit a traditional hammam for a budget scrub and steam session — try Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a local neighborhood hammam (entry + kessa scrub: 50–80 MAD / ~$5–8). End the evening with a quiet dinner at a local Moroccan restaurant away from the tourist center.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the hotel: café au lait and msemen with honey (20–30 MAD).
meals.lunch: Street food lunch: a sandwich of kefta or tuna from a medina snack shop (15–25 MAD / ~$1.50–2.50) plus fresh-squeezed juice.
meals.dinner: Local restaurant dinner: try Restaurant Al Baraka or a similar medina eatery — pastilla (pigeon or chicken pie), harira soup, and mint tea for 60–90 MAD (~$6–9).

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Youssef Madrasa and Saadian Tombs are must-sees for history lovers. Book the hammam visit in the late afternoon for a relaxing end to a busy sightseeing day. Carry a small daypack with water — March can be warm (18–24°C / 64–75°F).

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (6:00–7:00 AM) from Marrakech for the Sahara Desert — join a budget shared group tour/minibus to Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes). This is the most cost-effective option at 250–400 MAD (~$25–40) per person one-way, or book a 2-day/1-night shared group desert tour for 600–900 MAD (~$60–90) all-inclusive. The route passes through the stunning High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m). Stop at Aït Benhaddou — a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones (free to walk around the exterior, small fee to enter ~10 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley, passing kasbahs, palm oases, and dramatic desert landscapes. Stop in Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') for lunch and a brief walk past the Taourirt Kasbah (exterior free). Continue east through Skoura and Tinghir toward the Todra Gorge or directly toward Merzouga depending on tour route. Arrive in the Merzouga/Erg Chebbi area by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a budget desert camp near the Erg Chebbi dunes. Mount camels for a 45–60 minute sunset camel trek into the dunes (included in most group tours). Watch the sunset over the Sahara from the top of a sand dune — one of Morocco's most magical experiences. Spend the night in a traditional Berber desert camp with dinner, music around the campfire, and stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure or packed snacks for the road.
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch in Ouarzazate or a small town along the route: tagine set menu at a local restaurant (40–60 MAD / ~$4–6).
meals.dinner: Included in desert camp package: traditional Berber dinner — tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, bread, and mint tea around the campfire (included in tour price).

day_by_day.notes: Book the shared desert tour in advance from Marrakech — many budget guesthouses and agencies offer this. Recommended agencies: Sahara Expedition, Desert Majesty, or ask at Hotel Aday for recommendations. Bring warm layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C (41–50°F). Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a headscarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the dunes and watch the sunrise over the Sahara — an unforgettable, bucket-list moment. Take photos, explore the dunes on foot, and enjoy the silence of the desert. After breakfast at camp, explore the village of Merzouga on foot — visit the local market, interact with Berber families, and see the salt lake (Dayet Srji) nearby where flamingos sometimes gather in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional activities near Merzouga (budget-friendly): visit a Gnawa music village, explore a fossil shop (the region is famous for trilobite fossils), or take a short quad bike ride on the dunes (100–150 MAD / ~$10–15 for 30 minutes). Begin the return journey to Marrakech via shared minibus/group tour, taking a slightly different route through the Ziz Valley and Erfoud (known for date palms and fossil markets).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech late evening (around 21:00–22:00) after the long but scenic return drive. Check back into Hotel Aday. Grab a light late dinner near the hotel and rest — you've earned it after two days of desert adventure.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp: Moroccan bread, olive oil, jam, eggs, and mint tea.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside café en route: harira soup and bread (15–20 MAD) or a sandwich.
meals.dinner: Late-night simple meal near the hotel: a bowl of harira and msemen from a street stall near Jemaa el-Fna (20–30 MAD / ~$2–3).

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is long (8–10 hours with stops) — bring snacks, a good book or downloaded music/podcasts, and a neck pillow. The scenery through the Atlas Mountains at different times of day offers completely different perspectives. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in and recover from the desert trip. After a leisurely breakfast, visit the Majorelle Garden (entrance 150 MAD / ~$15 — the priciest attraction but worth it for garden lovers), a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Alternatively, for a free option, visit the Menara Gardens (free entry) with its olive groves and iconic pavilion reflecting pool — a peaceful escape from the Medina bustle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gueliz neighborhood (Marrakech's modern French-built ville nouvelle) for a change of pace from the Medina. Browse the Marché Central for fresh local produce, olives, spices, and affordable souvenirs. Visit the Cyber Parc Arsat Moulay Abdeslam (free) — a pleasant garden with free Wi-Fi. Head back to the Medina for final souvenir shopping in the souks — look for argan oil, leather goods, Berber rugs, and spices at fair prices.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a rooftop dinner with Medina views — try Nomad Restaurant (budget-friendly rooftop, mains 80–120 MAD / ~$8–12) or Café des Épices overlooking the spice square. End the evening with a final stroll through Jemaa el-Fna, soaking in the atmosphere one last time. Enjoy a traditional Moroccan mint tea ceremony at a café.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café: café au lait, croissant, and fresh orange juice (25–35 MAD).
meals.lunch: Marché Central area: fresh fruit, olives, and a sandwich from a local deli (20–30 MAD / ~$2–3).
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant treat: Moroccan pastilla, lamb tagine, or vegetable couscous with mint tea — 100–150 MAD (~$10–15) for a memorable final Marrakech dinner.

day_by_day.notes: The Majorelle Garden gets very crowded by midday — go early if you plan to visit. The YSL Museum next to Majorelle is 100 MAD extra if interested in fashion history. Saturday is market day in many Medina neighborhoods — great for authentic local shopping. Start packing tonight if your flight is tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — enjoy a slow breakfast and soak in the riad atmosphere of Hotel Aday. Take a final walk through the quieter Sunday morning Medina streets — the souks are calmer and more photogenic without the crowds. Visit any remaining sights you may have missed: the Dar Si Said Museum (Museum of Moroccan Arts, entrance ~30 MAD / ~$3) or the Maison de la Photographie (entrance ~50 MAD / ~$5) for stunning historical photos of Morocco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time: if afternoon flight, check out of hotel, store luggage at reception, and spend remaining time at a café near Jemaa el-Fna. Pick up last-minute souvenirs — ras el hanout spice blend, argan oil, or a small Berber carpet. Head to Marrakech Menara Airport (petit taxi: 70–100 MAD / ~$7–10). If evening flight, enjoy a final lunch and leisurely afternoon before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Marrakech with incredible memories of the Medina, Sahara dunes, Atlas Mountains, and Moroccan culture. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a beloved local café: Moroccan pancakes (baghrir) with honey and argan oil, mint tea (25–35 MAD).
meals.lunch: Final Moroccan meal: a classic chicken or lamb tagine with preserved lemon and olives at a medina restaurant (50–70 MAD / ~$5–7).
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the plane — grab a snack before departure if needed.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security at Marrakech Menara Airport. Petit taxis are metered — insist on the meter or agree on a price before getting in. Duty-free at the airport has good argan oil and spice sets if you forgot souvenirs. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights): 2,500–3,500 MAD (~$250–350 USD) per person, including accommodation, food, transport, and activities.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport transfer or petit taxi (~80–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and take a short stroll around the immediate Derb Sidi Bouloukat alley to get your bearings. The Medina at night has a magical atmosphere with lantern-lit streets.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a light snack from a 24-hour street vendor near Jemaa el-Fna square (~10 min walk) – try a msemen flatbread or harira soup for 15–25 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Confirm your hotel has 24-hour reception for late check-in. Exchange some currency at the airport (ATMs available). Rest well – big days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: After a hearty riad breakfast, begin exploring the heart of Marrakech. Visit the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square (5-min walk from hotel) in the morning when it's calm and photogenic. Then head into the souks – explore Souk Semmarine, Souk des Épices (Spice Square), and the dyers' quarter. Hire a local guide from the square for ~150–200 MAD for 2 hours to navigate authentically and avoid touts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD) – a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with ornate tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), royal mausoleums dating to the 16th century hidden for centuries behind a wall.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a massive open-air spectacle – snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Wander the square and soak in the UNESCO-listed atmosphere. End the evening with a rooftop mint tea at Café de France or Café Argana overlooking the square.

meals.breakfast: At Hotel Aday or a nearby café – traditional Moroccan breakfast with msemen, amlou (almond-argan dip), honey, and mint tea (~30–50 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in the Mellah area – try a tagine with preserved lemon and olives or couscous at a spot like Restaurant Haj Brik (~60–90 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at one of the food stalls on Jemaa el-Fna – try merguez sausages, grilled kefta, snail soup, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~50–80 MAD total). Adventurous and authentic!

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Medina streets are cobblestone and uneven. Bargaining in the souks is expected; start at 40–50% of the asking price. March weather in Marrakech is pleasant (~18–22°C), ideal for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Koutoubia Mosque and its gardens (non-Muslims cannot enter but the exterior and gardens are beautiful and free). Then head to the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) housed in a 19th-century palace, showcasing Moroccan art and artifacts. Nearby, visit the Ben Youssef Medersa (entry ~70 MAD), a breathtaking 14th-century Islamic college with intricate zellij tilework and carved stucco – one of Morocco's finest examples of Moorish architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short taxi ride (~20 min, ~30 MAD) to the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum complex. The Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD) is a stunning botanical garden with cobalt-blue buildings, designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Visit the adjacent Berber Museum (included in ticket). The YSL Museum (entry ~100 MAD, separate) is worth a visit for design lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Gueliz neighborhood (New City) for a change of pace – browse art galleries and modern boutiques. Enjoy a relaxed evening dinner in Gueliz before returning to the Medina.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or at Café des Épices near the spice square – fresh juices, pastries, and coffee (~40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Majorelle Garden – try Café Bousafsaf or a nearby café for a Moroccan salad plate and fresh juice (~70–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Al Fassia in Gueliz – a renowned women-run restaurant serving authentic Fes-style Moroccan cuisine. Try the pastilla (pigeon pie) or lamb with prunes (~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Majorelle Garden tickets online in advance – it sells out, especially in spring. The garden is best visited in the afternoon when morning crowds thin slightly. Keep your hotel key card handy as Medina navigation can be tricky after dark.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (~7:00 AM) on a pre-booked 3-day Sahara desert tour (widely available from ~1,800–2,500 MAD per person including transport, accommodation, and camel trek). The route heads southeast through the dramatic High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m). Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou – a spectacular fortified ksar (mud-brick citadel) used as a filming location for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia. Explore the kasbah on foot (~1.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through the Valley of Roses (Dadès Valley) and the dramatic Dadès Gorge with its towering red rock formations. Stop for photos at the famous 'monkey fingers' rock formations. Pass through Boumalne Dadès and continue toward the Draa Valley, passing kasbahs and palm oases.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Merzouga (gateway to Erg Chebbi dunes) by late afternoon/early evening. Mount camels for a 1-hour sunset trek into the Sahara dunes – one of the most memorable experiences in Morocco. Watch the sun set over the golden dunes. Spend the night at a mid-range desert camp with private tents, traditional Berber dinner, and live music around the campfire under a spectacular star-filled sky.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure (~included or 40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Ouarzazate or near Aït Benhaddou – try a local restaurant for a tagine and Moroccan salad (~80–120 MAD, often included in tour packages)
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp – included in most tour packages. Expect harira soup, tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, and mint tea around the campfire (~included in tour)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara tour 1–2 weeks in advance through your hotel or a reputable agency like Sahara Expedition or Desert Majesty. Bring warm layers – desert nights in March can drop to 5–8°C. Pack sunscreen, sunglasses, a headscarf for the dunes, and a power bank. The drive is long (~9–10 hours total) but the scenery is extraordinary.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (~5:30 AM) to climb the dunes and watch the Sahara sunrise – an unmissable, otherworldly experience. The shifting colors from deep purple to gold are breathtaking. Take photos, meditate, or simply absorb the silence. Return to camp for breakfast. Optionally, try sandboarding on the dunes before departure (~50–100 MAD extra if not included).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart the desert camp and begin the return journey. Stop at the Todra Gorge – a stunning narrow canyon with 300-meter-high rose-colored cliffs, perfect for a short hike along the river. Local Berber guides offer 1-hour walks through the gorge (~50–80 MAD). Continue driving through the Ziz Valley with its vast palm grove stretching for kilometers.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight stop in Ouarzazate – the 'Hollywood of Morocco.' Check into a mid-range riad or hotel (included in tour package or ~300–500 MAD independently). Visit the Atlas Film Studios (entry ~80 MAD) if time permits – the world's largest film studio where countless epics were filmed. Stroll the Taourirt Kasbah at sunset (entry ~20 MAD).

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp – traditional Berber breakfast with bread, olive oil, honey, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Todra Gorge – fresh trout from the river is a local specialty (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ouarzazate at Restaurant Chez Dimitri (a historic institution since 1928) or a local riad restaurant – try lamb mechoui or chicken with preserved lemon (~120–180 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge is best in the afternoon when sunlight streams into the canyon. Ouarzazate is a pleasant, relaxed town – a nice contrast to the intensity of Marrakech's Medina. If your tour ends in Merzouga, arrange a shared grand taxi or private transfer back (~400–600 MAD).

day_by_day.morning: Depart Ouarzazate and return to Marrakech via the scenic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass. The drive takes approximately 3.5–4 hours. Stop at Berber villages along the way to browse local argan oil cooperatives and buy authentic souvenirs directly from producers (argan oil, rose water, saffron). Arrive back in Marrakech by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your final afternoon in Marrakech revisiting your favorite spots or exploring what you missed. Consider a visit to the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) – a 16th-century palace once described as one of the world's most beautiful, now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the walls. Alternatively, book a traditional hammam experience at Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a mid-range hammam (~150–250 MAD for the full scrub and massage experience) – the perfect way to refresh after desert travel.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Marrakech – splurge slightly on a memorable dinner at a traditional riad restaurant. Explore the souks one last time for any remaining shopping. End the night with a rooftop cocktail (fresh juice if preferred) watching the Medina lights twinkle.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Ouarzazate before departure – included in accommodation or at a local café (~40–60 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch upon return to Marrakech – try Nomad restaurant near the Spice Square for modern Moroccan cuisine with a rooftop terrace (~120–160 MAD)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at Dar Yacout or Le Tobsil – iconic Marrakech riad restaurants with live Gnawa music, multiple-course Moroccan feast, and stunning courtyard ambiance (~350–500 MAD per person, worth the splurge on the last night)

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam and farewell dinner in advance. The hammam is best experienced in the late afternoon after the dusty return journey. If shopping in the souks, remember to bargain and compare prices across multiple stalls. Keep some MAD for tips and last-minute purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely final morning in Marrakech. Have a slow breakfast at the hotel or at a nearby café. Take a peaceful morning walk through the quieter Medina streets before the crowds arrive – the early morning light on the ancient walls is magical. Visit any last sights: the Mouassine Fountain, the Chrob ou Chouf Fountain, or simply wander and get beautifully lost in the labyrinthine alleys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, use the afternoon for last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks (leather goods, Berber rugs, lanterns, spices, argan products). Pack your bags and check out of Hotel Aday. Head to the airport with plenty of time – allow 1.5 hours before departure. Petit taxi to the airport costs ~80–100 MAD.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Morocco with incredible memories of ancient medinas, golden Sahara dunes, mountain passes, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or at a café – savor the mint tea, msemen, and amlou one last time (~30–50 MAD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a souk café or grab a sandwich and fresh juice for the road (~40–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Marrakech Menara Airport is about 6 km from the Medina – roughly 15–20 minutes by taxi. Arrive at least 2 hours before international flights. Declare any argan oil or food products at customs if required. Keep a small amount of MAD for the taxi and tips, and exchange remaining currency at the airport. Shukran (thank you) and safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Late arrival day. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from Marrakech Menara Airport to Hotel Aday in the Medina. A dedicated concierge will greet you at arrivals with a name board. Settle into your riad-style suite and enjoy a welcome mint tea and traditional pastries prepared by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In-flight or airport transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival (22:30). After check-in, unwind with a light welcome spread arranged by the hotel – Moroccan dates, msemen flatbread, argan oil dips, and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Rest and prepare for the journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: On board or at airport
meals.lunch: On board or at airport
meals.dinner: Welcome in-room spread at Hotel Aday upon arrival – dates, msemen, Moroccan pastries, and mint tea (arranged by hotel concierge)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport pickup with Hotel Aday before departure. Confirm your room is ready for late check-in. Keep Day 2 morning light to recover from travel fatigue. Tip: exchange a small amount of currency (MAD) at the airport for immediate needs.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a premium Moroccan breakfast at the hotel rooftop terrace. Then, embark on a private guided walking tour of the Medina – explore the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square in the morning calm before the crowds arrive, visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior), and stroll through the historic souks of spices, leather, and lanterns with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Bahia Palace (a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture) followed by the Saadian Tombs – two of Marrakech's most historically significant sites, both within walking distance of the hotel. Enjoy a private tour with an expert historian guide who provides cultural context beyond the standard tourist narrative.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the rooftop of a luxury riad bar overlooking the Medina skyline. Dinner at La Maison Arabe – one of Marrakech's most celebrated fine-dining establishments, offering a curated tasting menu of refined Moroccan cuisine including bastilla, slow-cooked lamb tagine, and orange blossom desserts in an opulent courtyard setting.

meals.breakfast: Rooftop breakfast at Hotel Aday – fresh-squeezed orange juice, msemen, amlou (almond-argan dip), Moroccan honey, hard-boiled eggs, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café des Épices in the Rahba Kedima spice square – Moroccan salads, harira soup, and fresh lemonade with a view over the souks
meals.dinner: La Maison Arabe – premium Moroccan tasting menu with wine pairing (approx. 800–1,200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book La Maison Arabe well in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina. The Bahia Palace and Saadian Tombs are within 10–15 minutes' walk from Hotel Aday. Hire a licensed private guide through the hotel concierge to avoid unofficial touts.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum (Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech). Arrive early (opening at 08:00) to enjoy the cobalt-blue garden in peaceful morning light before tour groups arrive. The YSL Museum offers a world-class exhibition on fashion, art, and Morocco's influence on the designer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Musée de Marrakech housed in the stunning Mnebhi Palace, then explore the Ben Youssef Madrasa – a 14th-century Islamic college considered one of the most beautiful buildings in North Africa, with intricate zellij tilework, carved stucco, and cedar woodwork. Followed by a private hammam and spa experience at a luxury riad spa (e.g., Les Bains de Marrakech) – traditional kessa scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Nomad Restaurant – a contemporary Moroccan rooftop restaurant with a modern take on traditional flavors. Try the lamb mechoui, preserved lemon chicken, and their signature Moroccan cocktails. The rooftop offers stunning views over the Medina at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Aday rooftop breakfast
meals.lunch: Al Fassia Aguedal – an all-female-run institution serving authentic Fassi (Fez-style) Moroccan cuisine; try the pigeon pastilla and lamb with prunes
meals.dinner: Nomad Restaurant, Derb Aarjane, Marrakech – modern Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views (approx. 400–700 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Majorelle Garden tickets online in advance – they sell out quickly. The hammam session should be booked 24 hours ahead through the hotel concierge. Musée YSL entry is approximately 100 MAD. March weather in Marrakech is pleasant (18–24°C), ideal for garden visits.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (07:00) by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the Sahara Desert – the journey takes approximately 8–9 hours via the spectacular Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m altitude) through the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou – a breathtaking 11th-century fortified ksar (village) used as a filming location for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia. Private guided tour of the ksar with a local Berber historian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley – a lush palm-lined oasis stretching for miles through dramatic desert landscapes. Stop in Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') for a brief visit to the Atlas Film Studios. Continue toward Zagora or Merzouga (depending on chosen Sahara camp location). Arrive at the desert edge by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Mount private camels (or opt for a 4x4) for a golden-hour ride into the Erg Chebbi or Erg Chigaga dunes. Arrive at your luxury desert camp – a premium glamping experience with private ensuite tents, Persian rugs, and lantern-lit pathways. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner under a canopy of stars: harira soup, mechoui lamb, couscous, and Moroccan pastries. Live Gnawa music and drumming around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast prepared by Hotel Aday before departure – Moroccan pastries, fruit, and thermos of mint tea for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional restaurant in Aït Benhaddou village – tagine with local bread and fresh salads
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber feast at the luxury desert camp – harira, mechoui lamb, couscous royale, and Moroccan sweets under the stars

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day (~8–9 hours driving). Depart no later than 07:00 from Marrakech. Ensure the private driver is booked through a reputable luxury operator. Bring layers – desert nights in March can drop to 5–8°C. Luxury desert camps (e.g., Scarabeo Camp, Erg Chigaga Luxury Camp, or Azalai Desert Lodge) must be booked months in advance. Confirm camp has private bathroom facilities.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (05:30) for a private sunrise camel or 4x4 ride to the top of the highest dune to watch the Sahara sunrise – one of the most extraordinary natural spectacles on Earth. Return to camp for a full Moroccan breakfast served in your private tent or the open-air dining pavilion. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a guided walk with a Tuareg desert guide to learn about desert survival, navigation by stars, and Saharan flora.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby desert oasis village – visit a traditional Berber family home for an authentic tea ceremony and learn about nomadic desert life. Optional 4x4 desert excursion into the deeper dunes with your private guide. Return to camp for a midday rest during the warmest hours. Enjoy a poolside lunch (if camp has pool) or a shaded terrace meal.
day_by_day.evening: Second night in the luxury desert camp. Private sunset aperitif on a dune crest with chilled Moroccan rosé or fresh juices. Stargazing session with a telescope provided by the camp – the Sahara offers some of the clearest night skies in the world. Dinner at camp: slow-cooked lamb tagine with apricots and almonds, Moroccan salads, and traditional mint tea ceremony.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at camp – msemen, amlou, fresh fruit, eggs, Moroccan honey, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the desert camp – Moroccan salads, grilled vegetables, fresh bread, and lemonade
meals.dinner: Gourmet Berber dinner at camp – lamb tagine with apricots, couscous with seven vegetables, and pastilla au lait dessert

day_by_day.notes: Bring high-SPF sunscreen, a wide-brimmed hat, and sunglasses – the desert sun is intense even in March. Temperatures can reach 28–32°C midday. Stay hydrated. The sunrise experience is the highlight of the entire trip – do not miss it. Confirm stargazing equipment availability with the camp in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise at the dunes, then depart the desert camp by 08:00 for the return journey to Marrakech via a different scenic route – through the Todra Gorge (dramatic 300-meter-high canyon walls) and the Dades Valley ('Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs'). Stop for a private guided walk through the Todra Gorge with a local Berber guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the rose-growing region of El Kelaa M'Gouna (famous for its annual Rose Festival). Stop at a local rose water distillery for a private tour and tasting. Continue through the Skoura palm grove and visit the historic Kasbah Amridil – one of Morocco's most photographed kasbahs. Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hotel Aday. Freshen up and enjoy a final luxury dinner at Le Tobsil – a legendary Marrakech institution set in a 17th-century riad, offering a lavish multi-course Moroccan feast with live Andalusian music. The experience includes bastilla, multiple tagines, couscous, and an elaborate dessert spread in an enchanting candlelit courtyard.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional restaurant in Tinghir near the Todra Gorge – fresh trout (a local specialty), Berber bread, and tagine
meals.dinner: Le Tobsil, Marrakech – legendary multi-course Moroccan feast with live music (approx. 700–1,000 MAD per person, all-inclusive)

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is approximately 7–8 hours with stops. Depart the desert camp no later than 08:00. Le Tobsil requires advance reservation and operates on a set-menu basis – confirm dietary requirements when booking. This is an ideal final celebration dinner. Book Le Tobsil at least 2 weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Enjoy a leisurely rooftop breakfast at Hotel Aday. Last-minute luxury shopping in the souks – visit the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) for antique silver jewelry, the leather souk for handcrafted bags, and the carpet souk for premium Berber rugs. A private shopping guide from the hotel can help negotiate fair prices and identify authentic artisan pieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxing afternoon at a luxury spa for a final hammam treatment and argan oil massage (e.g., Spa at La Mamounia or Selman Marrakech). Alternatively, visit the El Badi Palace ruins – a 16th-century palace of extraordinary scale with panoramic views from the ramparts, and the attached Museum of Moroccan Arts. Enjoy a final mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the Djemaa el-Fna.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Dar Yacout – a spectacular palace restaurant set in a 1,001 Nights-style riad with rooftop cocktails, a labyrinth of candlelit rooms, and a sumptuous Moroccan feast. Private transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for departure (confirm flight time and arrange transfer accordingly).

meals.breakfast: Leisurely rooftop breakfast at Hotel Aday – full Moroccan spread with fresh-squeezed orange juice, pastries, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Grand Café de la Poste – a colonial-era brasserie with Moroccan-French fusion cuisine; try the Moroccan-spiced lamb burger or the seafood pastilla
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout – iconic palace dining experience with rooftop cocktails and multi-course Moroccan feast (approx. 900–1,300 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm airport transfer time based on your departure flight. Allow at least 3 hours before flight for transfer and check-in. Pack any purchased argan oil, spices, or ceramics carefully in checked luggage. Dar Yacout requires advance reservation. Consider purchasing a premium gift box of Moroccan argan oil, rose water, and spices from a reputable shop as a souvenir.

query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March
